text: For the choirmaster. A psalm of the sons of Korah.
Clap your hands, all you peoples; shout to God with cries of joy!
For the LORD Most High is to be feared, a great King over all the earth.

versions.text: For the LORD Most High is awesome, a great King over all the earth.
versions.explanation: נוֹרָא is a passive participle meaning "feared, awe-inspiring." In modern English "awesome" has weakened to a casual compliment, which flattens the sense of holy dread. "To be feared" (or "awe-inspiring") preserves the reverential force and still reads smoothly aloud.

text: He subdues peoples under us, and nations beneath our feet.
He chooses our inheritance for us, the pride of Jacob, whom he loves. Selah
God has ascended amid shouts of joy, the LORD amid the blast of the ram's horn.

versions.text: God has ascended amid shouts of joy, the LORD amid the sound of the trumpet.
versions.explanation: שׁוֹפָר is the ram's horn, not a metal trumpet (חֲצֹצְרָה). "Blast of the ram's horn" is more precise and gives a stronger rhythmic close to the line for oral reading.

text: Sing praises to God, sing praises! Sing praises to our King, sing praises!
For God is King of all the earth; sing praises with a skillful song.
God reigns over the nations; God is seated on his holy throne.
The nobles of the peoples gather with the people of the God of Abraham; for the shields of the earth belong to God—he is highly exalted.

versions.text: The nobles of the peoples are gathered as the people of the God of Abraham; for the shields of the earth belong to God—he is highly exalted.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has no preposition before עַם, so "as the people of the God of Abraham" supplies an interpretive identification that goes beyond the text. Rendering it "with the people of the God of Abraham" (as many read the line) is less committal and reads naturally. A footnote could note that "the shields of the earth" refers to the earth's rulers and protectors.
